chapter_title: Concerning the Alms, that [ ... ] life in the Church.
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by institutional/almsgiving material about the holy church, elect/catechumens, and polemic about other sects (PASTORAL), wrapped in a brief hagiographic opening (FRAME). The oldest substrate appears as a self-contained cosmological sequence (¶7–¶10) describing the Living Soul’s ascent through the sun and moon (Light-givers) and the final rest of the Light-givers in the Land of Light. The ‘good earth / good tree’ analogy is explicitly anchored to catechumens/church and therefore functions as editorial application rather than cosmos→cosmos mapping.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic scene-setting (‘Once again… The enlightener sat… says to his disciples’), functioning as compilation frame, not teaching.

Institutional/polemical application: alms in ‘every sect’, ‘their catechumens’, and the ‘holy church’ as the only valid locus; cosmos→community identification dominates (editorial present-world mapping).
Defines ‘holy church’ ‘in two forms: in the brothers and the sisters’ and treats alms’ redemption via the church—church-institutional register, not cosmological exposition.
Seam-like continuation stressing catechumens as the church’s ‘place of rest’; institutional dependency logic (church↔catechumens) indicates later ecclesial application, not substrate cosmology.

Though cast as a correspondence/parable (‘good earth… gardener… good tree… fruit’), the mapping is explicitly to ‘the assembly of catechumens’ (cosmos/nature → contemporary church category), so it functions as editorial application rather than core substrate.
Explicitly applies the parable to ‘the [holy] church’ and catechumens as its support/rest; this is institutional extension of the analogy (editorial graft).

paragraphs.core_text: Likewise this [liv]ing Sou[l] that today is set in mixture; for it wishes to [as]cend and go to the house of its people, but it kn[ow[s a]nd understands that it has no open door in all the powers of heaven and earth. For they are its oppression that [ ... ] it everywhere. Indeed, it has no open door except the sun and the moon themselves, the Light-givers of the heavens [ ... / ... ] they become the place of rest for it. And they become a door that opens for it [in] the coming forth, and (the soul) comes out through them to the country of the household of i[ts] people.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological mechanics: mixture → ascent; ‘powers of heaven and earth’, sun and moon as ‘door’/‘place of rest’. ‘today’ is a minor deictic, but the mapping stays within cosmic architecture (no church categories).

paragraphs.core_text: Again, further in, also the Light-givers of the heavens have no place of rest amongst all the powers of heaven; except for the Lan[d] of Light, that has indeed been theirs for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-internal hierarchy: Light-givers vs. powers of heaven; final rest in the Land of Light. Pure cosmos→cosmos statement.

paragraphs.core_text: So, thus the Living Soul is purified of all afflictions; and they provide a rest for it, and open a door that opens to the house [of] its people.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative cosmological soteriology in mechanistic terms (purification/rest/door) without ecclesial application or citation.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, it is the case that the Lan[d] of Lig[ht] will become the final receiver for the Light-givers of [the] heavens, and they will rest themselves therein and rule in it [for] ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Closes the cosmological chain: Light-givers’ eschatological station in the Land of Light; structural, non-institutional voice.

Editorial ‘again’ applies the preceding ‘place of rest’ logic to ‘holy church’, ‘alms of the catechumens’, and concludes with both resting in the Land of Light; cosmos is used to validate institutional relationships (church↔catechumens), marking late application.
